Metadata.title: Roberto Moraes | Software Engineer & IT Manager
Metadata.description: Hands-on software engineer and technical leader. I lead teams, build high-performance Go backends, manage cloud infrastructure across AWS and GCP, and bring observability and DevOps practices to mission-critical systems.

About.title: About
About.mainTitle: From dev to manager without leaving the terminal
About.bio: I started as a full-stack developer and now lead the technology function at a company with international operations. Along the way, I learned that effective leadership means staying close to the work, so I continue to build backends, configure cloud infrastructure, and make sure every system can withstand production load. I own delivery from code through production deployment.
About.bioExtended: I have delivered projects for Hospital Sírio-Libanês, Grupo Bandeirantes, and international hotel chains, with an emphasis on measurable performance, resilient infrastructure, and effective teams. I stay hands-on: I write and review code, configure infrastructure, and make technical decisions—often on the same day.

band-news-bandsports.title: Grupo Bandeirantes
band-news-bandsports.shortDescription: Led the full rebuild of 6+ Grupo Bandeirantes portals, modernizing a high-traffic media platform with zero downtime.
band-news-bandsports.description: I led the mission-critical modernization of the Band News, BandSports, Arte 1, Sabor e Arte, TerraViva, and Agro+ portals. I coordinated design, engineering, and infrastructure teams while keeping the group's executive leadership aligned throughout. The migration also included a strategic content-distribution partnership with Vivo.
band-news-bandsports.challenge: Modernize six high-traffic media portals at the same time without disrupting service for millions of users, while coordinating multiple teams and maintaining architectural consistency.
band-news-bandsports.solution: A shared architecture with Next.js on the frontend, Go on the backend, and NestJS for supporting microservices. AWS WAF provided edge security, while elastic load balancing and progressive deployments enabled automated rollback.
band-news-bandsports.impact: Six portals modernized with a forward-looking architecture, enterprise-grade security, and the capacity to handle audience spikes during elections and live sporting events.
highlights: Direct coordination across design, frontend, backend, and infrastructure teams
Migration of 6 portals without downtime
WAF and edge security configured on AWS
Ongoing alignment with Grupo Bandeirantes executives
Strategic partnership with Vivo for content distribution
Final stack: Next.js + Go + NestJS + AWS

caseStudy.problem: The Grupo Bandeirantes portals ran on legacy stacks that were costly to maintain, delivered inconsistent performance, and struggled to scale for audience spikes such as elections and sports broadcasts.
caseStudy.solution: I designed a modern, shared architecture that allowed each portal to be deployed independently while reusing core components. The Go + Next.js stack delivered fast server rendering with consistently low latency.
caseStudy.robertoRole: I served as technical lead: I defined the architecture, coordinated four squads in parallel, negotiated timelines with executive leadership, and tracked every rollout. During critical sprints, I worked directly in the code to resolve performance bottlenecks.
keyDecisions: Selected Go for high throughput and predictable latency
Adoption of gradual (canary) deployment to avoid downtime
AWS WAF for DDoS protection in high-audience events
lessonsLearned: Legacy system migration requires constant communication with non-technical stakeholders
Gradual deployment is non-negotiable for high-visibility systems
results: Six portals modernized on an accelerated schedule

hospital-sirio-libanes.title: Hospital Sírio-Libanês
hospital-sirio-libanes.shortDescription: End-to-end architecture and engineering for a digital hospitality platform. Its Go backend handles 20M+ requests per month at 6ms average latency.
hospital-sirio-libanes.description: I led the backend, cloud infrastructure, and native application from architecture through production. I designed a high-availability platform for one of Latin America's largest hospital complexes, integrating the Tasy system, Unicast streaming with Widevine DRM, and a native Kotlin application for Android TV.
hospital-sirio-libanes.challenge: Build a resilient platform for real-time hospital operations—from streaming content to patient rooms through integrations with the Tasy hospital management system—while maintaining near-zero latency.
hospital-sirio-libanes.solution: Backend in Go (Fiber) optimized for maximum throughput, with auto-scaling orchestration in GCP (Cloud Run). Distributed cache with Redis (92% hit rate), persistence in PostgreSQL, and observability via Prometheus. Native Kotlin app with Jetpack Compose and Media3 for Android TV.
hospital-sirio-libanes.impact: A stable production platform handling 20M+ monthly requests at 6ms average latency, with infrastructure ready for healthcare audits and expansion to additional hospital units.
highlights: Built the backend and cloud infrastructure end to end without external vendors
Go + Fiber: chosen for low latency and high throughput
Integration with Tasy hospital system for patient data
Unicast streaming with Widevine DRM (premium content protection)
Native Kotlin/Jetpack Compose app for Android TV
Monitoring with Prometheus and real-time alerts
Cloud Run with auto-scaling on GCP

caseStudy.problem: Sírio-Libanês needed a digital hospitality platform for its patients that integrated real-time information from Tasy, content streaming with DRM protection, and an intuitive interface on room TVs.
caseStudy.solution: I designed and built the full stack: a high-performance Go backend, auto-scaling infrastructure on GCP, Redis caching for low-latency responses, and a Kotlin Android TV application with Widevine-protected streaming.
caseStudy.robertoRole: I owned the entire technical stack across backend, infrastructure, and mobile. As technical lead, I also defined the architecture, coding standards, and observability strategy. The need for ultra-low latency in a hospital environment drove the decision to use Go.
keyDecisions: Go + Fiber for performance: 6ms average latency
Redis as cache layer: 92% hit rate reduced load on PostgreSQL
Widevine DRM for premium content protection
Cloud Run for auto-scaling without managing servers
lessonsLearned: In healthcare, reliability comes before features
Observability is not optional. Prometheus saved nights of sleep
Integration with legacy systems (Tasy) requires obsessive documentation

fiesta-americana.title: Fiesta Americana Resort
fiesta-americana.shortDescription: Led a cross-border hospitality project that unified Unicast streaming and coaxial broadcast in a single platform.
fiesta-americana.description: I led a global initiative with engineering teams distributed across multiple time zones. The team built a native Kotlin application that brings cable TV signals (coaxial broadcast) and digital Unicast streaming together in a single interface on each guest-room TV.
fiesta-americana.challenge: Deliver a first-of-its-kind hardware-software solution for hospitality while aligning complex decoding engineering with stakeholders across continents and cultures.
fiesta-americana.solution: Cross-cultural project governance tailored to each time zone, combined with deep integration between hardware decoders (TV boxes and USB dongles) and native Android TV frameworks. The result unified two transmission models in one experience.
fiesta-americana.impact: The platform gave the hotel chain a differentiated guest experience by unifying transmission technologies that had previously operated as separate systems.
highlights: Teams distributed in multiple countries and time zones
Cross-cultural communication with international stakeholders
End-to-end ownership of schedule, quality, and delivery
First-of-its-kind native app combining Unicast and broadcast
Hardware integration: TV Box + coaxial signal via USB Dongle
Over-the-air and cable TV in the same hospitality app interface

caseStudy.problem: International hotel chains had two separate systems for TV: one for cable channels (coaxial) and another for digital streaming. Guests had to switch between TV inputs, creating a fragmented experience.
caseStudy.solution: I coordinated the development of a Kotlin app that decodes both signals simultaneously, presenting everything in a unified interface with integrated EPG. Hardware integration required custom drivers for USB dongles.
caseStudy.robertoRole: I led the international project end to end: aligning stakeholders across countries, defining the roadmap, managing risks, and ensuring quality. My Android TV engineering experience helped the team validate key architecture decisions.
keyDecisions: Use of USB dongles for coaxial signal capture (innovative solution)
Sprints adapted to different time zones
lessonsLearned: International projects require triple the documentation
Hardware integration has much longer test cycles than pure software
results: First hospitality app to unify broadcast and Unicast
Successfully deployed across an international hotel chain
